blocks.text: Mouse events are similar to keyboard events. There are some differences, though.

There are other event classes that can be used for handling
        mouse events, for instance `Gtk::EventControllerMotion` and
        `Gtk::EventControllerScroll`.

Many signal handlers don't return a `bool`.
        You can't stop those events from propagating.

The event classes that handle mouse events are also useful for handling
    events from touchscreens. There are also many subclasses of
    `Gtk::EventController` which are only (or mainly) useful
    for touchscreens. Examples: `Gtk::GestureRotate`,
    `Gtk::GestureZoom`, `Gtk::GestureSwipe`,
    `Gtk::GestureLongPress`.
This is an expanded version of the simple keyboard events example.
